text:
Predicates:
CanRegisterToVote(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateInElection(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Gazprom ::: Gazprom.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegisterToVote(x) → ParticipateInElection(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the election.
CitizenUS(x) → CanRegisterToVote(x) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote.
CitizenUS(x) ∨ CitizenTaiwan(x) ::: A person either has US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir does not hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir is not a manager at Gazprom.
EkaterinaCanRegisterOrVladimirManager ::: (CanRegisterToVote(Ekaterina)) ∨ (Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom)) ::: Ekaterina can register or Vladimir is a manager.
Conclusion:
CanRegisterToVote(Ekaterina) ∨ Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the election or Vladimir is a manager at Gazprom.
